entities.summary:
Gaspar de Ávalos de la Cueva (1485–1545), also named Gaspar Dávalos de la Cueva, was a Spanish Roman Catholic bishop and cardinal. He played a pivotal role in the Counter-Reformation within the Catholic Church.

As Bishop of Málaga from 1527 until his death, he implemented numerous reforms aimed at strengthening the Catholic faith among the population.

De la Cueva's tenure saw the establishment of the Congregation for the Evangelical Schools, which focused on promoting Catholic education in Spain. He also contributed to the compilation of the Index Librorum Prohibitorum (Index of Prohibited Books), a list of books deemed heretical or objectionable by the Church.

De la Cueva's legacy extends beyond his administrative reforms; he was also an influential figure in the theological debates surrounding the Eucharistic theology and the sacraments. His writings on these subjects continue to be studied by scholars today.

In a broader sense, de la Cueva's efforts during this period reflect the complex web of religious, political, and social forces that shaped the late medieval landscape. This era was marked by widespread religious strife, as the Protestant Reformation challenged traditional Catholic teachings and practices.
